questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I really wanted a University that was strong in my field of study (Biology and Pharmacology)

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very much as inspected and one of the best 4 months of my life! I cannot recommend this enough. A semester at any foreign university would be exciting but I have been really happy with my 4 months at UofT.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy if you could find it on your own, but if not you needed help it wasnt easy to get.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: No assistance was issued to exchange students upon arrival.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Impossible - I wasnt interested but I heard it was nearly impossible for the exchange students who tried.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is amazing but quite expensive. If you are 3 people living together you can get some great apartments for the semester for roughly 7500 kr/mdr/person in downtown/financial districts. These are the best districts in town and I have really enjoyed living here! You can find a bunch of them on Airbnb but dont wait until last minute!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Great if you had the money, but tough finding something cheap.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You get a T-card (studiekort) once you arrive on campus and this is one you need to identify yourself when taking exams. There wasnt any other kind of registration other than registrering for courses on their university portal.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: With a bit of persistence I got the ones that I wanted - even if they say that you dont have the prerequisites for a course, you can more often than not convince them that you do by showing them transcripts froom your courses at UCPH.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They are very strict on the registration deadlines so be aware of those!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very interesting courses - they have something for every niche and very competent professors teaching. The way of study is very different from UCPH with very limited reading before class, but instead a lot of lecture hours.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
Course are in either on these levels: 
100: 1st year    200: 2nd year.   300: 3rd year     400: 4th year.
As a bachelor you can take courses from either category.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More lectures but less reading than UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
CSC108: Introduction to Computer Programming
PCL200: Drugs and the Brain
HMB300: Neurobiology of behaviour
PCL475: Neuropsychopharmacology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Both of these were very interesting and had very competente professors being the best in their field:
HMB300: Neurobiology of behaviour
PCL475: Neuropsychopharmacology

questions.answer: Everything is more expensive than in Denmark!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Sports were great with lots of opportunities for different preferences!!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything you can imagine

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed the rural running club!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Weekend trip to Montreal and a walk through the Distillery District in Toronto

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy - much like europe

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just talk with the ones you are sitting with at lectures! People are usually very nice.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: not really

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Canadians are very nice!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Remember to use the city as you are living in a real city and things happen all the time around you. Just taking a stroll in the different neighborhoods of Toronto (or down by the water) is amazing through the different seasons. Also, try attending a fratparty - that is part of the culture.
2) Dont bring a lot of clothes! The rumor is really true - your wardrobe triples when being on exchange! Especially because UofT has a sick merchstore where you can buy everything imagineable.
3) Get a ESTA so you can go on a weekend trip to New York! It is very close by and quite cheap as well.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have fun, remember to socialize with fellow students and be conscious of the different papers needing to get into the country. You need a visa and maybe a study permit as well as being able to prove vaccination.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people and have lectures with some of the wisest people in my field of research.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The cold!! - even though it has been unusually nice weather, it really gets cold during the winter in Canada! But the winter is beautiful as well - just remember a sweater.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
